messages:
acme-cs: Hey team — intermittent partial messages from chat in prod since ~2026-03-04. Clients see responses truncating mid-sentence, then socket stays open. Happening on websocket only (client uses native ws). Sample request-id: rq_20260304_9f3a2d. Logged average latency normal. Can we triage?

alex_k: Thanks — can you paste the full request-id(s) and approximate timestamps? Also which region/cluster?

acme-cs: Sure — request ids: rq_20260304_9f3a2d, rq_20260304_9f3a3e. Timestamps UTC: 2026-03-04T21:12:03Z and 2026-03-04T21:14:11Z. Region: eu-west-1. Client is behind Fastly-based edge.

ranya: Noted. Can you reproduce with a simple wscat session so we can rule out client-side buffering? If not, can you capture a websocket frame dump (ngrep/wireshark) around the timestamps?

acme-cs: We couldn't reproduce locally. I can run ngrep on the staging proxy. Example ngrep command we plan to run:

```
ngrep -d any -W byline 'Host: api.redwood.ai' tcp and port 443
```

and capture with tcpdump: `tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w ws_dump.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443`

alex_k: Good. Also please send the raw client logs (ws send/recv frames) and the server-side request IDs you listed. We want the server response headers for those requests. If possible, export the ws frames as base64 from the client.

acme-cs: Attaching a short snippet of the client debug log (redacted):

```
[21:12:03.123] WS CONNECT -> wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
[21:12:03.456] SEND: {"type":"start","request_id":"rq_20260304_9f3a2d","messages":[...]}
[21:12:04.789] RECV: {"type":"delta","chunk":"Hello, I'm a"}
[21:12:04.790] RECV: {"type":"delta","chunk":"n AI assistant who"}
[21:12:04.791] RECV: {"type":"delta","chunk":" helps with..."}
[21:12:04.792] RECV: {"type":"final","chunk":""}  <-- here the client sees socket stay open but no more chunks
```

jorge: That pattern looks like possible proxy-level TLS reassembly or intermediate buffering. Can you also try disabling Fastly (direct origin) briefly for a repro? If you can't, we can look at our edge logs for the request ids.

maria: @alex_k @jorge I'll pull edge logs for rq_20260304_9f3a2d and rq_20260304_9f3a3e from eu-west-1 and check for any chunk truncation or upstream disconnects.

support-bot: Action items template:
- Collect: full client logs + base64 ws frames
- Collect: ngrep/tcpdump pcap around timestamps
- Collect: server edge logs (request ids above)
- Try: repro with direct-to-origin or wscat and report results
- Run: `redwood-debug-collect --request-ids rq_20260304_9f3a2d,rq_20260304_9f3a3e --include=edge,serving,network --out=debug_bundle.tar.gz`

acme-cs: Running debug collect now. Quick question: is there a specific flag to include Fastly request ids in the bundle?

alex_k: Use `--include=fastly-headers` for that. Also include any Fastly logs you can from your account. If you upload debug_bundle.tar.gz somewhere (S3 or our secure upload), share the link here or DM it.

acme-cs: Uploaded to temporary S3: https://s3.amazonaws.com/acme-support/debugs/ws_debug_20260304.tgz (expires in 24h).

ranya: Thanks — I'll download and start a quick pass for reassembly anomalies. If we see a proxy cutoff we'll ask infra to pull TCP-level packets.

jorge: If we need a live repro window, can you schedule a 30-min window when you can flip to direct origin? It'd speed root-cause.

acme-cs: We can do a 30-min window tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll post when it's live.

maria: Great. Meanwhile I'll attach the edge log snippet I already fetched for rq_20260304_9f3a2d: 

```
2026-03-04T21:12:04.788Z edge_id=eu-1 req_id=rq_20260304_9f3a2d client_ip=52.12.34.56 upstream_status=200 upstream_bytes=3422 upstream_conn_close=false chunked=true
2026-03-04T21:12:04.793Z edge_id=eu-1 req_id=rq_20260304_9f3a2d client_ip=52.12.34.56 upstream_status=200 upstream_bytes=3422 upstream_conn_close=true chunked=false note="upstream half-close"
```

alex_k: Interesting — edge shows upstream_conn_close toggling right after last delta. Could be the serving instance closed after sending final event but client didn't receive final chunk. I'll triage serving logs next.

support-bot: Reminder: keep PII out of uploads. Use redwood-secure-upload for sensitive bundles. :lock:

acme-cs: Thanks. I'll sanitize and re-upload to redwood-secure-upload.

ranya: One more ask — can you capture a short ngrep output and paste first 20 lines here (no full pcap) so we can verify frame boundaries quickly?

acme-cs: Pasting ngrep sample: 

```
T 52.12.34.56:55342 -> 34.201.13.7:443
  TLSv1.3 Record Layer: Application Data, length: 512
  TLSv1.3 Record Layer: Application Data, length: 128
  TLSv1.3 Record Layer: Alert, length: 2
```

jorge: That Alert line could indicate an abrupt TLS close. Could be Fastly or client. If it repeats in multiple traces, looks like a middlebox.

maria: I've pulled serving host logs for that instance id. There's an open ticket to correlate with the SLO-based connection limits. Attaching small snippet: 

```
[2026-03-04T21:12:04.790Z] serving[rq_20260304_9f3a2d] INFO chunk: "Hello, I'm an AI assistant who"
[2026-03-04T21:12:04.792Z] serving[rq_20260304_9f3a2d] INFO final_event_sent true
[2026-03-04T21:12:04.792Z] serving[rq_20260304_9f3a2d] WARN connection: half-close from upstream
```

alex_k: Ok — evidence points to an upstream half-close right after final event. Next steps: if the customer can repro during the direct-origin window, we'll confirm whether Fastly is the culprit. If reproduces direct->origin then it's likely serving runtime.

acme-cs: Understood, will test tomorrow 09:00 UTC and respond here with results and the sanitized bundle link. Appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
